B_sl_before_tp.expect: magnifier: exit at SL 95. Chart OHLC identical to scenario A.

C_tp_touched_before_limit_entry.expect: magnifier: no exit on the entry bar (105 printed pre-entry); trade closes at SL 95 on the settling bar. whole-bar: entry 100 then H106 >= 105 -> TP same bar.

D_subbar_gap_entry.expect: magnifier: entry fills at the gapped sub-bar open 101.2. whole-bar: chart bar opens 98 < 100 with H103, so a path-blind engine fills at the stop level 100.

E_short_tp_before_sl.expect: magnifier: short entry ~96 then TP 91 before SL 101.

L_trail_peak_then_dip.expect: peak 104 FIRST, then a 2.5 retrace. A 2.00 trail armed at 104 stops out at 102.

M_trail_dip_then_peak.expect: the dip to 101.5 comes BEFORE the peak 104, so the trail is never armed above the dip and there is no exit. Chart OHLC identical to L.

F_tie_same_subbar.expect: one M1 bar spans 94->106, touching SL 95 and TP 105 inside a single sub-bar. Pins the intrabar tie policy; magnifier and whole-bar may agree by accident, so read this row against F's sibling scenarios.

G_exact_touch.expect: the path reaches exactly 105 then exactly 95 — no overshoot. Pins inclusive (<=/>=) trigger comparison at the level itself.

H_empty_bucket.expect: the scenario bar's M1 rows are dropped after generation, so its bucket is empty: that one chart bar must fall back to chart OHLC and be counted in dataFallbackBars while its neighbours stay magnified.

I_trail_retrace.expect: monotonic rise to 104 then a 2.5 retrace, then a deeper drop on the settling bar. Trailing-stop activation and offset are pure path questions the chart bar cannot answer.

J_exit_gap.expect: the take-profit at 105 is never traded — the path gaps 99 -> 106.5 between two M1 rows. Pins exit gap-fill pricing (fill at the sub-bar open, not at the level).

K_two_roundtrips.expect: TP, then a drop through SL, then a second TP — multiple magnified round trips in one run.
